title: Éire
capsule: Éire is the Irish-language name and constitutional title for Ireland as established by the Constitution of Ireland (Bunreacht na hÉireann) enacted on 29 December 1937 under Taoiseach Éamon de Valera, replacing the Irish Free State with a sovereign state that removed the Crown from all domestic functions and claimed nominal authority over the whole island. The state remained formally within the Commonwealth until the Republic of Ireland Act 1948 came into force on 18 April 1949, when the term 'Republic of Ireland' became the official description for external purposes while 'Éire' (or 'Ireland' in English) remained the constitutional name. Ireland joined the United Nations in 1955 and the European Economic Community in 1973, becoming a founding member of the eurozone in 1999.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The state's territorial extent (the island of Ireland minus the six counties of Northern Ireland) is unambiguous and internationally recognized from 1922 onward; the 1938 start date reflects the constitutional renaming rather than a boundary change.
